(Section)

Among that is His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Never came to them a messenger but that they used to mock him (11). Thus We let it enter into the hearts of the criminals (12)﴾

This meaning occurs in the Qur'an in two places: this one is the first, and the second is in Surah al-Shu'ara' in His saying: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it. Thus We have let it enter into the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: "He let shirk enter into the hearts of the deniers just as the bead is threaded onto the string."

Abu Ishaq said: "That is, just as He did to the criminals who mocked the messengers before them, so He lets misguidance enter into the hearts of the criminals." They differed regarding the referent of the pronoun in His saying ﴿We let it enter (naslukuhu)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We let shirk enter," and this is also the view of al-Hasan.

Al-Zajjaj and others said: "It is misguidance (al-dalal)."

Al-Rabi' said: "It means mockery (al-istihza')."

Al-Farra' said: "Denial (al-takdhib)." These statements all go back to one thing: denial, mockery, and shirk are all, in reality, their own actions, and He has informed that it is He, Glorified is He, who let it enter into their hearts. However, I have a reservation about these statements, for the apparent sense is that the pronoun in His saying ﴿they do not believe in it﴾ refers to the same thing as the pronoun in His saying ﴿We let it enter﴾. Thus it is not correct that the meaning is "they do not believe in shirk, denial, and mockery." Those statements are only sound if the referents of the two pronouns differ, whereas the apparent sense is that they are one and the same. So "those who do not believe in it" are those into whose hearts He let it enter, and it is the Qur'an.

If it is said: what is the meaning of His letting it enter into their hearts while they deny it?

It is answered: He let it enter into their hearts in this state, meaning: We let it enter while they were not believing in it, so it entered their hearts as deniers of it, just as it entered the hearts of the believers as affirmers of it. This is what those who said the one who let it enter into their hearts is denial and misguidance meant, but they explained the verse by its meaning, for when it enters their hearts as deniers of it, denial and misguidance have entered their hearts.

If it is said: what is the meaning of His causing it to enter their hearts while they do not believe in it?

It is answered: so that the proof of God be established against them by it. It entered their hearts and they knew that it is true, yet they denied it; it did not enter their hearts in the manner of one who affirms it, believes in it, and is pleased with it. Their denial of it after it had entered their hearts is greater disbelief than their denial of it before it entered their hearts, for one who denies the truth after knowing it is worse than one who denies it without having known it. So reflect upon this, for it is part of the understanding of tafsir. And God is the Granter of success toward what is correct.

(Fa'idah)

The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasures﴾ contains a treasure among treasures, namely that every thing is sought only from the One who has its treasures, and the keys to those treasures are in His hands; and seeking it from other than Him is seeking from one who does not possess it and has no power over it.

His saying ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾ contains a great treasure, namely that every aim, if it is not directed for His sake and does not connect to Him, is then perishing and cut off, for there is no final end but with Him. The final end is only to Him toward whom all matters end, so they end in His creation, His will, His wisdom and His knowledge. He is the goal of every sought thing and every beloved thing. Whatever is not loved for His sake, its love is toil and torment; every deed not intended for His sake is wasted and void; and every heart that does not reach Him is wretched, veiled from its happiness and success. Thus everything that is to be desired from Him is gathered in His saying ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasures﴾, and everything for which He is to be desired is gathered in His saying ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾. So beyond Him, glorified is He, there is no goal to be sought, and beneath Him there is no goal at which the final end ends.

Under this lies a great secret of the secrets of Tawhid, namely that the heart does not settle, nor become tranquil and at rest, except by arriving at Him. Everything other than Him that is loved and desired is desired for the sake of something else, and the desired object loved for its own sake is only the One, to whom is the final end. It is impossible for the final end to be two, just as it is impossible for the origin of creation to be from two. Whoever's final end of love, desire, will and obedience is other than Him, that will be voided for him and will vanish from him and leave him at the moment he most needs it. Whoever's final end of love, desire, fear and seeking is He, glorified is He, will attain His blessings, pleasure, delight and happiness forever and ever.

The servant is constantly fluctuating between the rulings of commands and the rulings of calamities. He is in need, indeed compelled, to (divine) help at the time of commands and to (divine) gentleness at the time of calamities. In proportion to his standing by the commands he obtains gentleness at the time of calamities. If his standing by the commands is complete, outwardly and inwardly, he attains gentleness outwardly and inwardly; and if he stands by their forms without their realities and inner dimensions, he attains gentleness outwardly, while his share of inner gentleness diminishes. If you ask, "What is inner gentleness?" It is what comes to the heart at the time of calamities of tranquility, calm, the removal of anxiety, agitation and distress, so that it humbles itself before its Master, submissive and abject, looking to Him with its heart, at rest in Him with its spirit and inner self, its contemplation of His gentleness toward it occupying it from the severity of the pain it is in, and its knowledge of His good choice for it, and that it is a pure servant over whom its Master executes His rulings, whether He is pleased or angered, veiling it from witnessing that. If He is pleased, it attains good pleasure; if He is angry, its portion is anger. This inner gentleness is the fruit of that inner dealing; it increases with its increase and decreases with its decrease.

If it is said: what wisdom is there in letting Iblis remain until the end of time while the messengers die?

The answer is that God has wisdom in this that human imaginations cannot contain. Among it: since He made him a test and a trial, through which the good is distinguished from the bad and His ally from His enemy, His wisdom required that he be kept alive so that the purpose intended by His creation would be achieved. Had He caused him to die, that purpose would have been lost. Likewise, His wisdom required that His enemies, the disbelievers, remain on earth until the end of time. Had He destroyed them entirely, the many wisdoms in letting them remain would have been nullified. Just as His wisdom required the testing of the father of mankind, it required the testing of his offspring after him through him. Thus happiness is attained by those who oppose and oppose him, and those who agree with and befriend Him gather to Him.

Another wisdom: since His forbearance and wisdom had preceded that he has no share in the Hereafter, and since he had earlier performed obedience and worship, He rewarded him for them in this world by granting him life in it until the end of time. Indeed, He does not wrong anyone for a good deed they have done. As for the believer, He repays him for his good deeds both in this world and in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, He repays him for the good deeds he did in this world, so that when he reaches the Hereafter, he has nothing left. This meaning is established in the Sahih (authentic collection) from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Another: his remaining alive was not an honor for him. Had he died, it would have been better for him, lighter for his punishment, and less for his evil. But because his sin grew grave through persistence in disobedience, disputing with the one who ought to be submitted to in His judgment, impugning His wisdom, vowing to seize His servants and turn them away from His worship, the punishment for his sin was the greatest punishment in proportion to its gravity. So he was left alive in this world and given respite, so that he would increase in sin upon sin, and thus deserve the punishment that is not suitable for anyone else. He becomes the head of the people of evil in punishment, just as he was their head in evil and disbelief. Since he is the source of every evil, from him it arises, and he is recompensed in the Fire with the like of his deed. Every punishment that descends upon the people of the Fire begins with him, then spreads from him to his followers, as a manifest justice or a far-reaching wisdom.

Another: in his dispute with his Lord he said: ﴿Have You seen this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few.﴾ God, glorified is He, knew that among the offspring there would be those unfit to dwell with him in his abode, and that they are fit only for what thorns and dung are fit for. So He left him to them, and said to him through the language of the divine decree (al-qadar, God's predetermined ordainment): "These are your companions and allies. Sit and wait for them. Whenever one of them passes by you, then do as you wish with him. Had he been fit for Me, I would not have given you power over him. I take as allies the righteous, who are fit for Me, and you are the ally of the criminals, who have become independent of My allegiance and of seeking My pleasure." The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾

As for the death of the prophets and messengers, it was not because of their humiliation before Him. Rather, it was so that they might reach the station of His honor, rest from the hardship and toil of this world, and be relieved of the suffering caused by their enemies and followers. It also allows the messengers after them to live, one messenger following another. Their death is therefore better for them and for the community. As for them, it brings them rest from the world and joining the Highest Companion in the most perfect pleasure and joy, especially since their Lord gave them the choice between remaining in this world and joining Him.

As for the nations, it is known that they did not obey them only during their lifetimes. Rather, they obeyed them after their deaths just as they obeyed them in life. Their followers did not worship them but worshipped God by following their commands and prohibitions. God is the Living who does not die. So there is much wisdom and benefit in their death, both for them and for the nations. Moreover, they are human beings, and God did not create humans in this world with a constitution suited to permanence. Rather, He made them successors on earth, one succeeding another. Had He let them remain, the benefit and wisdom in making them successors would have been lost, and the earth would have become too narrow for them. Death is therefore a perfection for every believer. Were it not for death, life in this world would not be pleasant, nor would its people find contentment in it. Thus the wisdom in death is like the wisdom in life.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 15, verse 41:

al-Hasan said: Its meaning is "a path leading to Me, straight." This allows two possibilities. The first is that he meant it is from the category of placing particles in the place of one another, so the particle "ʿalā" (on) takes the place of "ilā" (to).

The second is that he meant the explanation according to meaning, which is more fitting with the method of the early generation (al-salaf), namely: "a path that connects to Me." Mujahid said: "The truth returns to Allah, and His way is upon it; it does not deviate toward anything." This is like the statement of al-Hasan and clearer than it, and it is among the most correct things said about the verse. It has also been said that "ʿalayya" here indicates obligation (lil-wujub), meaning: upon Me is its clarification, its making known, and guiding to it. The two views are similar to the two views concerning the verse of al-Nahl, which is ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ [al-Nahl: 9]. The correct view regarding it is like the correct view regarding the verse of al-Hijr: that the direct path, which is the straight and balanced way, returns to Allah and leads to Him. Tufayl al-Ghanawi said:

*They passed on before us, the direct way being upon them,*
*and the turning of fates overturns men.*

That is: our passing is over them, and our arrival is to them. Another said:

*Those are the fates; whatever valley I have traversed,*
*my path is upon them, or their path is upon me.*

If it is said: were this meaning intended, the more suitable thing would be the particle "ilā," which denotes endpoint, not the particle "ʿalā," which denotes obligation. Do you not see that when He intended arrival He said, ﴿Indeed to Us is their return; then indeed upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25–26], and He said ﴿To Us is their return﴾ [Yunus: 70], and He said ﴿Then to their Lord is their return﴾ [al-An'am: 108], and when He intended obligation He said ﴿Then indeed upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 26], and He said ﴿Indeed upon Us is its gathering and its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 17], and He said ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾ [Hud: 6], and the like of these.

It has been said: in the particle "ʿalā" there is a subtle secret, which is the indication that the one who travels this path is upon guidance, and this is true, as He said concerning the believers, ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5], and He said to His Messenger ﵺ... 

[Note: the passage continues below as given.]

Correction for accuracy: the text continues as follows.

And He said to His Messenger (ﷺ) ﴿So rely upon Allah; indeed you are upon the manifest truth﴾ [al-Naml: 79]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Truth, His path is true, and His religion is true. So whoever keeps to the straightness of His path is upon the truth and guidance. Thus in the particle "ʿalā," on this meaning, there is what is not in the particle "ilā," so reflect upon it, for it is a wondrous secret.

And in the saying of the Exalted, ﴿He said: This is a path upon Me, straight﴾ [al-Hijr: 41], there is a third view, which is the view of al-Kisa'i, that it is for threat and warning, like His saying ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [al-Fajr: 14]. As he said: you say "your path is upon me" and "your passage is upon me" to one whom you want to inform that he will not escape you and cannot overcome you. The context rejects this, and it does not suit it for one who reflects on it, for it was said in reply to Iblis, who said, ﴿I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [Sad: 82–83]. So there is no way for me to mislead them, and no path for me over them.

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, affirmed that most completely, and informed that sincerity is a straight path upon Him. There is no authority for you over My servants who are upon this path, for it is a path upon Me, and there is no way for Iblis to this path, nor to hover around its precinct, for it is guarded and protected by Allah, so the enemy of Allah cannot reach its people.

Let the one who knows reflect upon this point with due reflection, and consider this meaning, and weigh it against the other two views, to see which is more fitting for the two verses, and closer to the intent of the Qur'an and the sayings of the early generation. As for al-Kisa'i's comparison of it to ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [al-Fajr: 14], the difference between them in context and indication is not hidden, so reflect on it. One does not say in a threat, "This is a straight path upon me," to one who does not travel it, and the path of the one threatened is not straight; he is not threatened by the straight path of Allah, and his path upon which he is is not straight with respect to Allah. So this view does not stand at all.

As for one who interpreted it as obligation, meaning: upon Me is the explanation of its straightness and guiding to it, the meaning is sound, but whether this is the intended meaning of the verse is open to question, because it is an omission in a place where there is no indication, and the omitted element is not established such that it is understood when omitted. This differs from the operator of the adverbial phrase when it occurs as a description, which is a familiar and well-known omission, so much so that it is never mentioned at all. When you say, "He has a dirham upon me" (lahu dirham ʿalayya), the omission is well known and familiar. But if you intended "upon me is its payment," or "upon me is its weight and safekeeping," or the like, and omitted it, it would not be permissible. This is similar to "upon me is its explanation," assumed in the verse, while what the early generation said is more fitting to the context and greater and more exalted of the two meanings.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Ahmad Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "These two are similar to His saying, ﴿Indeed upon Us is the guidance, and indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the former life﴾ [al-Layl: 12–13]." He said: "So these are three places in the Qur'an with this meaning."

I say: Most of the exegetes, regarding the surah "﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1]," mentioned only the meaning of obligation, namely: upon Us is the clarification of guidance from error. Among them are those who, regarding surah al-Nahl, mentioned only this meaning, such as al-Baghawi, while regarding al-Hijr he mentioned the three views. Al-Wahidi in his al-Basit mentioned the two meanings in surah al-Nahl. Our Shaykh chose the view of Mujahid and al-Hasan in the three surahs.

This is a disjunctive (munqati') exception, because those who follow you among the misguided (al-ghawin) did not enter into the category of those who are attributed to Him as servants ('ibad al-mudafin ilayhi), even though they do enter into the general category of servants (mutlaq al-'ibad). He informs about the meeting of their hearts and the meeting of their faces.

In the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) it is reported: "Their creation is upon the creation of one man, upon the form of their father Adam (peace be upon him), sixty cubits tall in the sky."

The proportion between this height and breadth is not hidden, for if one of them exceeded the other, moderation would be lost; the proportion of the creation would become height with thinness, or thickness with shortness, and both are unsuitable. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The Love of the People of Lot]

The second group, whose love Allah related, are the people of Lot (al-Lūṭiyyah), as the Most High said: ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing. He said, "Indeed these are my guests, so do not disgrace me. And fear Allah and do not humiliate me." They said, "Did we not forbid you from [dealing with] the worlds?" By Allah, it is the incurable disease and the deadly poison, which does not cling to a heart without the people finding it difficult to free it from its captivity, and its fire does not blaze in a soul without the creatures finding it hard to rescue it from that fire.

It has divisions:

At times it is disbelief: for one who takes his beloved as a rival (nidd) that he loves as he loves Allah. How much more so if his love is greater than the love of Allah in his heart? The sign of shirki, disbelieving love is that the lover prefers the pleasure of his beloved over his Lord. When the right of his beloved and his desire conflict with the right of his Lord and His obedience, he gives precedence to the right of his beloved over the right of his Lord, prefers his beloved's pleasure over his Lord's pleasure, gives to him the most precious thing he can offer, and gives to his Lord, if he gives at all, the worst of what he has. He exhausts his strength in pleasing his beloved, obeying him, and seeking closeness to him, and gives to his Lord, if he obeys Him, only the leftover time which his beloved has graciously spared from his hours.

So consider the condition of most lovers of forms, and you will find it corresponds to this. Then place their condition on one scale and their tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness) and their faith on the other scale, and weigh them with a weighing that pleases Allah and His Messenger and accords with justice. Often a lover among them openly states that union with his beloved is dearer to him than the tawhid of his Lord, as the wicked lover said:

"They sip from my mouth sips
Which are sweeter in it than tawhid."

And as the other wicked one declared that union with his beloved is more desirable to him than the mercy of his Lord, which has already passed.

Rather, [the beloved] has possessed their entire heart, so that he has become a pure slave in every respect to his beloved. And when will the one intoxicated by it sober up?"

So consider the condition of most lovers of forms, and you will find it corresponds to this. Then place their condition on one scale and their tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness) and their faith on the other scale, and weigh them with a weighing that pleases Allah and His Messenger and accords with justice. Often a lover among them openly states that union with his beloved is dearer to him than the tawhid of his Lord, as the wicked lover said:

"They sip from my mouth sips
Which are sweeter in it than tawhid."

And as the other wicked one declared that union with his beloved is more desirable to him than the mercy of his Lord, which has already passed.

Without doubt this love is among the greatest forms of shirk. Many of them openly declare that no place remains in their hearts for anyone other than their beloved at all. Rather, [the beloved] has possessed their entire heart, so that he has become a pure slave in every respect to his beloved. Thus he has accepted, in place of the worship of the Creator, may His majesty be exalted, the worship of a created being like himself. For worship ('ubūdiyyah) is the perfection of love and submission, and this one has exhausted the strength of his love, submission and humility toward his beloved, so he has given him the reality of worship.

There is no comparison between the corruption of this grave matter and the corruption of fornication (al-fāḥishah). For that is a great sin whose ruling is that of its like, whereas the corruption of this love is the corruption of shirk. Some of the knowledgeable shaykhs (ʿārifīn) used to say: "To be tested with fornication with that form is dearer to me than to be tested in it with a love in which my heart worships her and which preoccupies it from Allah."

Most of the exegetes (mufassirūn) from the early and later generations, indeed one does not know of any dispute among the early generation (al-salaf) about it, held that this is an oath by the life of the Messenger (ﷺ). This is one of the greatest of his virtues, that the Lord, mighty and majestic, swears by his life, and this is a distinction not known for anyone else.

Al-Zamakhsharī (d. 538 AH), however, did not agree with this, and he diverted the oath to refer to the life of Lot and to be a statement of the angels. He said: "It is by implied speech (ʿalā irādat al-qawl), meaning the angels said to Lot, peace be upon him: 'By your life, indeed they were wandering in their intoxication.'" But there is nothing in the wording that indicates either of the two matters. Rather, the apparent wording and its context only indicate what the early generation understood, not what the people of ta'ṭīl (denial of Allah's attributes) and i'tizāl (the Muʿtazilah) understood. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Labaʿamruka means wa-ḥayātika (by your life)," and he said: "Allah never swore by the life of any prophet other than him."

ʿUmur and ʿumr are the same word, except that they reserved the oath form for the one with a fatḥah [i.e., ʿamruka, with the vowel a], to establish the lighter form, because the oath is frequently repeated on their tongues. Also, ʿumr (life) is a particular life; it is a noble, great life, deserving that He swear by it because of its distinction over every lifespan of the children of Adam. There is no doubt that his life and his lifetime are among the greatest blessings and signs, so he is worthy to be sworn by, and swearing by him is more fitting than swearing by any other creature.

As for the Most High's words ﴿yaʿmahūn﴾, meaning they wander in confusion. Allah, glory be to Him, described the people of Lot as being in intoxication (sakrah) only because the intoxication of love is like the intoxication of wine, as the poet said:

"Intoxicated by the fracture of desire and the intoxication of wine,
And when will the one intoxicated by it sober up?"

Ibn al-Qayyim, *al-Tafsir al-Qayyim*, on Surah 15, verse 75 (Part 1 of 3)

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has praised *firasah* (discerning insight) and its people in several places in His Book. This is one of them.

*Al-mutawassimun* are those who discern (*mutafarrisun*) and who read the *simah*, which is the mark or sign. It is said: "I *tawassamtu* in you such-and-such," meaning "I discerned it in you," as if it were taken from *simah*. It is an elongated form (*fi'la'*) from *simah*, which means a sign.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would recognise them by their marks﴾. He also said: ﴿The ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their modesty; you recognise them by their marks﴾.

In al-Tirmidhi there is a hadith traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Beware the *firasah* of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾.

Abu al-Darda' used to say: "Beware the *firasah* of the scholars. Beware lest they bear witness against you a testimony that throws you on your faces into the Fire. By Allah, it is truly what Allah casts into their hearts."

I say: The origin of this in al-Tirmidhi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), is: "Beware the *firasah* of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾ [al-Hijr: 75].

[Section: The difference between *firasah* and *zann* (conjecture)]

The difference between *firasah* and *zann* is that *zann* may be right or wrong. It occurs with the darkness or light, purity or impurity, of the heart. For this reason Allah commanded avoiding much of it and informed us that some of it is sin.

As for *firasah*, Allah praised its people in His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) and others said: "That is, for those who discern." Allah also said: ﴿The ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their modesty; you recognise them by their marks﴾, and: ﴿And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would recognise them by their marks, and you would surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾.

True *firasah* belongs to a heart that has been purified, cleansed, and freed from defilements, and has drawn near to Allah. Such a person looks with the light of Allah that He has placed in his heart.

In al-Tirmidhi and others, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware the *firasah* of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah."

This *firasah* arises in him from his nearness to Allah. When the heart draws near to Allah, the obstacles of evil that prevent it from knowing and perceiving the truth fall away from it. It receives from a niche near to Allah in proportion to its nearness to Him. Light shines upon it according to its closeness, so it sees in that light what the distant and the veiled do not see. This is as established in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ), on the authority of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who said: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing by which he hears, his sight by which he sees, his hand by which he strikes, and his foot by which he walks. By Me he hears, by Me he sees, by Me he strikes, by Me he walks."

So Allah, glorified, informed us that the servant's drawing near to Him brings him His love. When He loves him, He becomes his hearing, sight, hand, and foot; he hears by Him, sees by Him, strikes by Him, and walks by Him. His heart thus becomes like a clear mirror in which the forms of realities appear as they truly are, so that his *firasah* rarely errs. When the servant sees by Allah, he sees the matter as it truly is; when he hears by Allah, he hears as it truly is. This is not knowledge of the unseen, for it is the Knower of the Unseen who casts the truth into a heart that is near to Him, rejoicing in His light and not occupied with the patterns of falsehood, fancies, and whisperings that would prevent the forms of realities from taking shape within it.

When light dominates the heart, it overflows onto the limbs and hastens from the heart to the eye, so that it sees with the eye of sight what the light perceives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to see his companions behind him in prayer just as he saw them in front of him. He saw Bayt al-Maqdis clearly while he was in Makkah, saw the palaces of Syria and the gates of Sana'a and the cities of Kisra while he was in Madinah digging the trench. He saw his commanders at Mu'tah when they were struck while he was in Madinah. He saw the Negus in Abyssinia when he died while he was in Madinah, so he went out to the place of prayer and led the funeral prayer for him. Umar saw Sariyah at Nahawand in the land of Persia, he and the armies of the Muslims while they were fighting their enemy, and he called out: "O Sariyah, the mountain!" A group from Madhhij, among them al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i, entered upon him, and he looked at him intently, lowered and fixed his gaze, and said: "Who is this?"

Malik ibn al-Harith said: He said, "What is with him? May Allah kill him! I see for the Muslims from him a grievous day."

ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd entered upon al-Hasan, and he said: "This is the lord of the youth, if he does not speak."

It is said that al-Shafi'i and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan sat in the Sacred Mosque. A man entered, and Muhammad said: "I discern that he is a carpenter." Al-Shafi'i said: "I discern that he is a blacksmith." They asked him, and he said: "I was a blacksmith, and today I am a carpenter."

Abu al-Hasan al-Busanji and al-Hasan al-Haddad entered upon Abu al-Qasim al-Manawi to visit him. On their way they bought apples on credit for half a dirham. When they entered upon him, he said: "What is this darkness?" They went out and said: "We do not know, perhaps it is because of the price of the apples." So they paid the price and returned to him. His gaze fell upon them, and he said: "Can a man come out of darkness this quickly?" He said: "Tell me about your situation." They told him the story. He said: "Yes. Each of you relied upon the other to pay the price, and the man was ashamed of you both when demanding payment."

Between Abu Zakariyya al-Nakhshabi and a woman there was a cause before his repentance. One day he was standing at the head of Abu ʿUthman al-Hiri, thinking about her affair. Abu ʿUthman raised his head to him and said: "Are you not ashamed?"

Shah al-Kirmani had excellent *firasah*; his discernment never erred. He used to say: "Whoever lowers his gaze from what is forbidden, restrains his self from desires, cultivates his inner self through constant vigilance (*muraqabah*), and outwardly follows the Sunnah, and accustoms himself to eating what is lawful, his *firasah* will not err."

There was a young man who accompanied al-Junayd and would speak about the thoughts that occur to people (*al-khawatir*). It was mentioned to al-Junayd. He said: "What is this that has been reported to me about you?" The young man said: "Let me form a belief." Al-Junayd said: "Form it." The young man said: "I have believed such-and-such." Al-Junayd said: "No." He said: "Then let me form a second belief." He said: "Form it." He said: "I have believed such-and-such." Al-Junayd said: "No." He said: "Then let me form a third." He said: "Form it." He said: "It is such-and-such." Al-Junayd said: "No." The young man said: "This is strange, and you are truthful. I know my own heart." Al-Junayd said: "You were right in the first, the second, and the third, but I wanted to test you, to see whether your heart would change."

Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz said: I entered the Sacred Mosque, and a poor man in two worn cloaks entered, asking for something. I said to myself: "This man is a burden on people." He looked at me and said: ﴿Know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him﴾. He said: I sought forgiveness silently in my heart, and he called out to me: ﴿And He it is who accepts repentance from His servants﴾.

Ibrahim al-Khawwas said: I was in the congregational mosque when a young man came, pleasant of fragrance, handsome of face, and of good dignity. I said to my companions: "It occurs to me that he is a Jew!" All of them disliked this. I went out, and the young man went out too. Then he returned to them and said: "What did the Shaykh say about me?" They were shy before him, but he insisted until they said: "He said you are a Jew." He came and fell upon my hand and became a Muslim. I said: "What is the reason?" He said: "We find in our book that the *siddiq* (truthful one) is never wrong in his *firasah*." I said: "I will test the Muslims, and I examined them. I said: If there is a *siddiq* among them, it is in this group. I was deceiving you. When this shaykh looked at me and discerned me, I knew he was a *siddiq*."

And Uthman ibn ʿAffan (may Allah be pleased with him): a man of the Companions entered upon him, having seen a woman on the road, and he had contemplated her beauty. Uthman said to him: "One of you enters with the trace of adultery clear upon his eyes." I said: "Has revelation come after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "No, but it is insight, proof, and true *firasah*."

This is the nature of *firasah*. It is a light that Allah casts into the heart, so a thing occurs to him and it is as it occurred to him, and it penetrates to the eye and sees what others do not see.

[Section: Wonders of *firasah*]

Among the wonders of *firasah* is what is reported of Ahmad ibn Tulun: that while he was in a gathering where he was relaxing, he saw a beggar in a worn garment. He placed a chicken in a loaf and some sweets and ordered one of the boys to give it to him. When it fell into his hand, he did not show joy and did not care for it. Ibn Tulun said to the boy: "Bring him to me." When he stood before him, he questioned him, and he answered well and was not shaken by his awe. He said: "Bring the papers you have with you, and tell me truthfully who sent you, for it is clear to me that you are a bearer of news." He brought the whips, and he confessed. Some of his companions said: "By Allah, this is sorcery!" He said: "It is not sorcery, but true *firasah*. I saw the evil of his condition. I sent him food that a satisfied man would eagerly eat, yet he did not rejoice at it nor stretch out his hand to it. I brought him, and he met me with firmness of heart. When I saw the shabbiness of his state and the firmness of his heart, I knew he was a bearer of news, and so it was."

One day he saw a porter carrying a large jar (*sinn*) and it was shaking beneath him. He said: "If this shaking were from the weight of the load, the porter's neck would have sunk into his shoulders, yet I see his neck protruding. I see nothing of this matter except from fear." He ordered the jar set down. In it was a girl who had been killed and cut up. He said: "Tell me about her condition." He said: "Four men in such-and-such house gave me these dinars and ordered me to carry this dead girl." Ibn Tulun struck him and killed the four.

He used to disguise himself and go round the city, listening to the recitation of the imams. He called his trusted man and said: "Take these dinars and give them to the imam of such-and-such mosque, for he is poor and his heart is occupied." He did so, and sat with him and was friendly with him. He found that his wife was in labour, and he had nothing he needed. He said: "He spoke truly. I knew the preoccupation of his heart from his many mistakes in recitation."

Among these: thieves took a great amount of money in the time of al-Muktafi, and al-Muktafi required the chief of police (*sahib al-shurtah*) to bring out the thieves or pay the value of the money. He used to ride alone and go about by night and day, until one day he passed through a deserted alley in one of the outskirts of the city. He entered it and found it unfamiliar, and found that it had no outlet. He saw on some of its doors many fish bones and vertebrae.

He said to a man: "What would be the price of this fish whose bones these are?" He said: "A dinar." He said: "The people of this alley cannot afford a buyer like this, for it is an alley clearly in disrepair beside the desert. No one lives in it who has anything he fears for, or who has wealth to spend this much from. This is nothing but a calamity, and it must be uncovered." The man thought this unlikely and said: "This is far-fetched thinking." He said: "Find me a woman from the quarter so I can speak with her."

He knocked on a door other than the one with the fish bones and asked for water. An old, weak woman came out. He kept asking for one drink after another while she gave it to him, and in the meantime he asked about the quarter and its people, and she told him, not aware of the consequences of this. Finally he said to her: "And who lives in this house?" He pointed to the one upon which were the fish bones. She said: "In it are five young men, ruddy-complexioned, who look like merchants. They have been staying there for a month. We do not see them by day except at long intervals. Each of them goes out on an errand and returns quickly. All day they gather, eat and drink, and play chess and backgammon. They have a boy who serves them. When night comes they go back to a house of theirs in al-Karkh, leaving the boy in the house to guard it. When it is dawn they come, and we are asleep and do not notice them." She said to the man: "Is this the description of thieves or not?" He said: "Yes." He immediately sent word, summoned ten men of the police, and brought them up onto the rooftops of the neighbours. He himself knocked on the door. The boy came and opened it.

The police entered with him, and not one of the people escaped. They were precisely the perpetrators of the crime.

Among these: one of the governors heard, on a winter night, a voice in a house asking for cold water. He ordered the house raided. They brought out a man and a woman. It was said to him: "How did you know?" He said: "Water is not cooled in winter. That is only a sign between these two."

One of the governors brought two suspects accused of theft. He ordered that a jug of water be brought. He took it in his hand and then deliberately threw it down so that it broke. One of them was alarmed, while the other remained steady and did not change. He said to the one who was alarmed: "Go." And he said to the other: "Bring the money." It was said to him: "How did you know that?" He said: "The thief has a steady heart and does not become alarmed. The innocent man thinks that if a mouse moved in the house, it would alarm him and prevent him from stealing."

[Section: The station of *firasah*]

Among the stations of "﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾" [al-Fatihah: 5] is the station of *firasah*.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern﴾ [al-Hijr: 75].

Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Those who discern." Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "The observers." Qatadah said: "Those who take lessons." Muqatil said: "Those who reflect."

These sayings are not contradictory, for whenever the observer looks at the traces of the dwellings of the deniers and their abodes, and at what their affair came to, it bequeaths to him *firasah*, lesson, and reflection.

Allah, the Exalted, said regarding the hypocrites: ﴿And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would recognise them by their marks, and you would surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. The first is the *firasah* of the sight and the eye; the second is the *firasah* of the ear and hearing.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, say: "He made their recognition by sight dependent upon His will, but He did not make their identification through the tone of their speech dependent upon any condition. Rather, He stated it as a fact emphasised by an oath, saying: 'and you would surely know them by the tone of their speech.'" That is the indirect allusion of speech, its implication and its intended meaning.

*Al-lahn* (tone, the manner of speech) has two kinds: correct and incorrect. The correct *lahn* is of two types. The first is *al-fitnah* (acuteness, perceptiveness). From this is the hadith: "Perhaps some of you are more eloquent in his argument than others." The second is allusion and indication, which is close to *kinayah* (allusion). From this is the saying of the poet:

"A speech sweet to me, and it is of what the listeners desire, is weighed out measure by measure. A correct utterance, and it changes at times in its tone, and the best speech is that which is in tone."

The third is corruption of speech in *i'rab* (grammatical inflection). Its reality is the alteration of speech from its proper form, either into an error or into a hidden meaning for which the word was not designed.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 15, verse 75 (part 2 of 3):

The point is that He, glorified is He, swore that they recognize it from the tone of their speech. For knowing a speaker and what is in his heart from his speech is closer than knowing him by his mark and what is on his face. The indication of speech upon the intention of its speaker and his inner state is clearer than the visible mark. Firasa (discernment, physiognomic insight) relates to both kinds, through sight and through hearing. In al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Beware of the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." Then he recited His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.﴾ [al-Hijr: 75]

[Section: The Types of Firasa]

Firasa is of three types. The first is the faith-based (iman), which is the one being discussed in this station.

Its cause is a light that Allah casts into the heart of His servant, by which he distinguishes between truth and falsehood, the present and the absent, and the truthful and the liar.

Its reality is that it is a thought that rushes upon the heart, negating what opposes it. It pounces upon the heart like the pouncing of a lion upon its prey. But the prey (farisa) is a form of fa'ila in the sense of maf'ula. The pattern of firasa is like the pattern of wilaya (authority), imara (command) and siyasa (governance).

This firasa is in proportion to the strength of faith. Whoever has stronger faith has sharper firasa.

Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz said: Whoever looks with the light of firasa looks with the light of truth, and the materials of his knowledge are with the truth, without error or heedlessness. Rather, it is a judgment of truth that flows upon the tongue of His servant.

Al-Wasiti said: Firasa is flickers of lights that shine in the hearts, and the establishment of knowing the totality of hidden secrets in the unseen, from unseen to unseen, until he witnesses things from the standpoint from which the Truth made him witness them, and so he speaks of the inner state of creation.

Al-Darani said: Firasa is the unveiling of the soul and the direct witnessing of the unseen, and it is among the stations of faith.

Someone was asked about firasa, and he said: They are spirits that move about in the malakut, overlooking the meanings of the unseen, and speaking of the secrets of creation with the speech of witnessing, not the speech of conjecture and supposition.

Amr ibn Nujayd said: Shah al-Kirmani had sharp firasa and never erred. He would say: Whoever lowers his gaze from what is forbidden, restrains his soul from desires, cultivates his inner self with watchfulness (muraqaba) and his outer self with following the Sunna, and accustoms himself to eating what is lawful, his firasa will not err.

Abu Ja'far al-Haddad said: Firasa is the first thought without an opposing counter-thought. If another thought of its kind opposes it, then it is a passing thought and self-talk.

Abu Hafs al-Nisaburi said: No one may claim firasa. Rather, one should beware of the firasa of others, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the firasa of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." He did not say: "Practise firasa." How can claiming firasa be valid for one who is in the position of guarding against firasa?

Ahmad ibn Asim al-Antaki said: When you sit with the people of truthfulness, sit with them in truthfulness, for they are spies of the hearts; they enter your hearts and leave from where you do not expect.

Al-Junayd was once speaking to the people, when a young Christian man in disguise stood before him and said: "O Shaykh, what is the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: 'Beware of the firasa of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah'?" Al-Junayd lowered his head, then raised it to him and said: "Embrace Islam, for the time of your Islam has come." So the youth embraced Islam.

It is said in some ancient books: Indeed, the siddiq's firasa never errs.

Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The most discerning of people are three: the Aziz regarding Yusuf, when he said to his wife: ﴿Honour his stay; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son.﴾ [Yusuf: 21]; the daughter of Shu'ayb when she said to her father about Musa: "Hire him," and Abu Bakr regarding Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he appointed him as successor. In another narration: and the wife of Pharaoh when she said: ﴿A delight of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son.﴾ [al-Qasas: 9]

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was the greatest of this Ummah in firasa, and after him Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. His instances of firasa are well known, for he never said of something "I think it is such-and-such" except that it was as he said. And it suffices as evidence of his firasa that his Lord agreed with him in well-known situations.

Sawad ibn Qarib passed by him, and Umar did not know him. He said: "My assumption has erred, or this man is a soothsayer, or he knew soothsaying in the Jahiliyya." When he sat before him, Umar told him this. He said: "Glory be to Allah, O Commander of the Believers, you have not addressed any of your companions with the like of what you have addressed me with." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "What we were upon in the Jahiliyya was greater than that. But tell me what I asked you about." He said: "You have spoken truly, O Commander of the Believers. I was a soothsayer in the Jahiliyya." Then he mentioned the story.

Likewise, Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, was truthful in firasa. Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I entered upon Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, and I had seen a woman on the road and had contemplated her beauty. Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "One of you enters upon me while the trace of fornication is evident in his eyes." I said: "Is it revelation after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "No, but it is insight, proof and truthful firasa."

The firasa of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, is the most truthful of firasa.

The root of this type of firasa is from the life and light that Allah, exalted is He, bestows upon whomever He wills of His servants, so the heart comes alive by it and is illuminated, and thus his firasa almost never errs. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose example is in darkness, never to emerge from it?﴾ [al-An'am: 122] He was dead through disbelief and ignorance, and Allah gave him life through faith and knowledge, and made for him, through the Qur'an and faith, a light by which he is guided among the people upon the right path, and by which he walks in darknesses. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The Second Type: The Firasa of Discipline and Hunger]

The second type of firasa is the firasa of discipline (riyada), hunger, staying awake, and seclusion. When the soul is stripped of obstacles, it acquires firasa and unveiling in proportion to its detachment. This firasa is shared between the believer and the disbeliever, and it does not indicate faith or sainthood (wilaya). Many ignorant people are deceived by it. The monks have well-known instances of it. It is a firasa that does not reveal any beneficial truth or any straight path. Rather, its unveiling is partial, of the same kind as the firasa of rulers, of interpreters of dreams, of physicians and the like.

Physicians have a well-known firasa from their skill in their craft. Whoever wishes to understand it should study their history and reports. Nearly half of medicine is truthful firasa, accompanied by experience. And Allah, glorified is He, knows best.

[Section: The Third Type: Physiognomic Firasa]

The third type of firasa is physiognomic (khalqiyya), which is the one physicians and others have written about. They infer character from form, because of the connection between them that the wisdom of Allah has established, such as inferring a small mind from an unusually small head, and from a large head, and from breadth of chest and the distance between its two sides, the breadth of character of its owner, his tolerance and expansiveness; and from narrowness, narrowness; from dull eyes and weak sight, the dullness of their owner and weakness of heart's warmth; and from intense whiteness of the eye mixed with redness, which is the shape, courage, boldness and shrewdness; and from roundness together with redness and frequent movement, treachery, deceit and cunning.

Most of the connection of firasa is with the eye, for it is the mirror of the heart and the title of what is within it. Then with the tongue, for it is its messenger and interpreter. And by inferring from its blueness together with the fairness of its owner, his inferiority; and from the loneliness seen upon it, the evil of what is within him and the corruption of his disposition.

Like inferring from excessive hair that is limp the dullness, and from excessive curliness the evil, and from moderation, the moderation of its owner.

The root of this firasa is that the moderation of form and appearance results from the moderation of temperament and spirit, and from its moderation arises the moderation of morals and actions.

In proportion to the deviation of form and appearance from moderation, deviation occurs in morals and actions.

This is when the soul is left to its nature.

But the owner of a moderate form and appearance acquires, through association and companionship, the morals of those he associates with and keeps company with, even if he is among the beastly animals. So he becomes among the most evil of people in morals and actions, and those habits become his nature, and it becomes impossible, or difficult, for him to move away from them.

Likewise, the owner of a form and appearance deviating from moderation acquires, through the company of the perfected and by mixing with them, noble morals and actions, which become for him like nature, for habits and practices produce qualities and morals.

So let one reflect on this point and not hasten to judge by firasa without it, for the judge in that case will often err. For these signs are causes, not necessary determinants, and their judgments may fail to follow due to the absence of a condition or the presence of an impediment.

The firasa of the one who discerns relates to three things: his eye, his ear, and his heart. His eye is for the features and signs; his ear is for speech, its explicitness and allusiveness, its literal and implied meaning, its implication, its indication, its tone and its faith, and the like. And his heart is for crossing over: inferring from what is seen and heard to what is hidden and inward, so that he passes beyond the outer surface, like the crossing of the money-assayers from the outer stamp and mint to the inner reality of the coin and examining it: is it genuine or adulterated? Likewise is the crossing of the discerning one from the outer appearance and bearing to the inner spirit and heart. So the ratio of his assessment of spirits from bodies is like the ratio of the money-changer's assessment of the jewel from the outer stamp and mint.

Likewise is the criticism of the people of hadith, for a chain of narration that appears as clear as the sun may pass over a fabricated text, and their critic extracts it, just as the money-changer extracts the adulteration from beneath the apparent silver.

Likewise is the firasa of distinguishing the truthful from the liar in his statements, actions and states.

Firasa has two causes. One is the keenness of the discerner's mind, the sharpness of his heart, and the goodness of his intelligence. The second is the manifestation of signs and evidences upon the one being discerned. When the two causes combine, the servant's firasa almost never errs. When both are absent, his firasa almost never succeeds. When one is strong and the other weak, his firasa is somewhere in between.

Iyas ibn Mu'awiya was among the greatest people in firasa, and he has well-known instances.

Likewise al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. It is said that he authored works on it.

I have witnessed from the firasa of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, wondrous matters, and what I did not witness of them is greater and greater still. The instances of his firasa would require a large volume.

He informed his companions of the Tatars' entry into Syria in the year 699 AH, and that the armies of the Muslims would be broken, and that Damascus would not see a general slaughter or a general captivity, and that the army's greed and intensity would be directed at wealth. This was before the Tatars had even resolved to move.

Then, in the year 702 AH, when the Tatars moved and aimed for Syria, he informed the people and the commanders that the defeat and rout would be upon them, and that victory and triumph belonged to the Muslims. He swore to this more than seventy oaths. He was told: "Say, if Allah wills." He said: "If Allah wills, as a certainty, not as a conditional." I heard him say that. He said: When they pressed me, I said: "Do not press me. Allah, exalted is He, has written in the Preserved Tablet that they will be defeated this time, and that victory belongs to the armies of Islam." He said: The sweetness of victory had made some of the commanders and soldiers covetous before they set out to meet the enemy.

And his partial firasa during these two events was like rain.

When he was summoned to the Egyptian lands and his killing was sought, after the cooking pots had been prepared for him and affairs had been turned against him, his companions gathered to bid him farewell. They said: "Letters have repeatedly come that these people are working to kill you." He said: "By Allah, they will never reach that." They said: "Will you be imprisoned?" He said: "Yes, and my imprisonment will be long. Then I will come out and speak the Sunnah (the prophetic way) before the people." I heard him say that.

When his enemy, the one nicknamed al-Jashankir, took over the kingdom, they informed him of this and said: "Now he has reached his aim from you." So he prostrated to Allah in gratitude and remained in prostration for a long time. He was asked: "What is the reason for this prostration?" He said: "This is the beginning of his humiliation and the departure of his might from now on, and the nearness of the end of his affair." It was asked: "When will this be?" He said: "The horses of the army will not be tied at al-Qurt until his state is overthrown." Then the matter happened just as he had told. I heard that from him.

He once said: "My companions and others enter upon me, and I see in their faces and their eyes matters that I do not mention to them."

I said to him, or someone other than me said to him: "If only you would inform them!" He said: "Do you want me to be an informant like the informants of the rulers?" I said to him one day: "If you treated us with that, it would be more conducive to uprightness and righteousness." He said: "You would not endure with me in that for a week, or he said: a month."

He informed me on more than one occasion of hidden matters specific to me, concerning what I had resolved upon, which my tongue had not uttered.

He also informed me of some great events that would occur in the future, without specifying their times. I have seen some of them while I await the rest.

What his senior companions witnessed of such things was many times over what I witnessed. And Allah knows best.

(Another section)

His saying: "And insight causes firasa (discernment) to grow, in meaning..."

He means that basira (inner insight) causes true firasa to grow in the land of the heart. It is a light that Allah casts into the heart, by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the truthful and the liar. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern.﴾ [al-Hijr: 75]

Mujahid said: "For those who practice firasa." In al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Beware of the firasa of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic," then he recited: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern.﴾ [al-Hijr: 75]

Al-tawassum (discerning by marks) is a form of tafa'ul derived from al-sima, which is the mark. The one who practices firasa is called mutawassim because he infers from what is witnessed to what is hidden, so he reasons from the seen to the unseen. For this reason Allah the Exalted specified these people for the signs and for benefiting from them, because they deduce from what they observe of them the reality of what the messengers informed of: the commands and prohibitions, reward and punishment. Allah inspired this to Adam and taught it to him when He taught him the names of everything. His descendants are his copies and his successors. Every heart is thus receptive to this, and it has it potentially. Through it proof is established, lessons are attained, and guidance is sound. Allah sent His messengers as reminders and alerters, and as perfecters of this readiness, with the light of revelation and faith. So that is added to the light of firasa and readiness, and it becomes light upon light. Insight is strengthened, the light grows and endures by the increase of its source and its continuance, and it keeps increasing until it is seen on the face, the limbs, the speech, and the deeds. Whoever does not accept the guidance of Allah and does not raise his head to it, his heart enters into coverings and veils, so it becomes dark and blind to insight. The realities of faith are then concealed from him, so he sees truth as falsehood, falsehood as truth, rectitude as error, and error as rectitude. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14] Al-rayn and al-rann are the dense veil that prevents the heart from seeing the truth and submitting to it.

Firasa varies according to the strength and weakness of insight, and it is of two kinds:

A lofty and noble firasa, specific to the people of faith; and a lowly and base firasa, shared between the believer and the disbeliever. The latter is the firasa of the people of riyada (spiritual discipline), hunger, sleeplessness, seclusion, and stripping the inner self of all kinds of preoccupations. These have the firasa of uncovering forms and informing of some worldly hidden matters, whose uncovering and reporting does not include perfection for the soul, nor purification, nor faith, nor knowledge. Their firasa does not go beyond these lowly matters, because they are veiled from the Truth, the Exalted. So their firasa does not ascend to distinguishing between His friends and His enemies, nor the way of these and those.

As for the firasa of the truthful, those who know Allah and His command: since their resolve is attached to the love of Allah, knowing Him, worshipping Him, and calling people to Him upon insight, their firasa is connected to Allah and linked to the light of revelation along with the light of faith. So it distinguishes between what Allah loves and what He hates, among persons, sayings, and deeds. It distinguishes between the wicked and the good, the one upon the truth and the one upon falsehood, the truthful and the liar. It knows the measures of readiness of those traveling to Allah, so it carries each person according to his readiness in knowledge, will, and action.

The firasa of these people is thus always revolving around uncovering the way of the Messenger and recognizing it, and extracting it from among all the other paths; and around uncovering the faults of the self and the diseases of deeds that hinder travel on the path of the messengers. This is the most noble kind of insight and firasa, and the most beneficial for the servant in his livelihood and his return.

[Section: The difference between humility (tawadu') and abasement (mahanah)]

The difference between humility and abasement is that humility arises from a combination of: knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, and recognition of His names, attributes, and majestic qualities, and magnifying Him, loving Him, and revering Him; and from knowing oneself in its details and the faults and defects of one's deeds. From all of that combined arises a disposition which is humility, and it is the breaking of the heart before Allah and the lowering of the wing of submission and mercy toward His servants. Such a person does not see for himself any virtue over anyone, nor does he see for himself any right with anyone; rather he sees the virtue of people over himself and their rights before him. This is a disposition which only Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bestows upon one whom He loves, honors, and brings near.

As for abasement (mahanah): it is baseness, lowliness, and the surrendering and debasing of the self in pursuit of its portions and desires, like the humility of the base people in attaining their desires, the humility of the one acted upon toward the one acting, and the humility of the seeker of any benefit toward the one from whom he hopes to attain his benefit. All of this is lowliness, not humility. Allah, the Exalted, loves humility and hates lowliness and abasement. In the Sahih, from him (ﷺ), it is related: "And it was revealed to me: Be humble, so that no one boasts over another and no one transgresses against another." Praiseworthy humility is of two types:

The first type: the servant's humility before the command of Allah, by complying with it, and before His prohibition, by refraining from it. The soul, seeking ease, lags behind in obeying His command, and various forms of refusal and fleeing appear from it, running away from servitude; and it persists in the face of His prohibition, seeking to obtain what has been forbidden. So when the servant lowers his self to the command and prohibition of Allah, he has become humble to servitude.

The second type: his humility before the greatness and majesty of the Lord, and his submission to His might and grandeur. Whenever his soul becomes proud, he remembers the greatness of the Lord, the Exalted, and His uniqueness in that, and His severe anger toward whoever disputes that with Him; so his soul humbles itself to Him, his heart breaks before the greatness of Allah, it finds rest in His awe, and it submits to His authority. This is the ultimate humility, and it necessitates the first, though not vice versa.

The truly humble person is one who has been granted both. And Allah is the One sought for help.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 15, verses 92–93:

Several of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: it refers to the statement "there is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and this is true.

For the entire question concerns it, its rulings, its rights, its obligations, and its requirements. No one is ever questioned except about it and about its obligations, its requirements, and its rights. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "There are two words about which the first and the last (of mankind) will be questioned: 'What did you used to worship?' and 'What did you answer the messengers?'"

So the question "What did they used to worship?" is a question about it itself, and the question "What did they answer the messengers?" is a question about the means and the path leading to it: whether they walked upon it and answered the messengers when they called them to it. Thus the whole matter returns to it.

A matter of this status deserves that fingers be clasped upon it, that it be held tightly with the molars, and that one grasp it as one grasps a live coal. It should not be taken with the tips of the fingers, nor should its excellence be sought as a secondary pursuit; rather, it should be made the greatest aim, and whatever else is sought is sought only as a surplus.

And Allah is the Granter of success; there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

(Lață'if) A Bedouin once heard a reciter recite the verse ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾ and prostrated. He was told, "This is not a verse of prostration!"

He replied, "I prostrated because of the eloquence of this speech."

[Section: The most perfect of creation is the one who fulfils all the levels of jihad]

The most perfect of creation in the sight of God is the one who fulfils all the levels of jihad. People differ in their ranks before God in proportion to their differing levels of jihad. For this reason, the most perfect and most honoured of creation before God was the seal of His prophets and messengers, for he fulfilled all the levels of jihad, strove for God with the striving due to Him, and undertook jihad from the time he was sent until God, Mighty and Majestic, took him. When there was revealed to him, ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn, and magnify your Lord, and purify your garments﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 1-4], he girded himself for the call and stood up for the sake of God with the most complete standing, and he called to God by night and by day, in secret and openly. When there was revealed to him, ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾ [al-Hijr: 94], he proclaimed the command of God without fear of the blame of any blamer, and he called to God the young and the old, the free and the slave, the male and the female, the red and the black, and the jinn and mankind.

When he proclaimed the command of God and openly called his people to the message, and denounced their gods and criticised their religion, their harm to him intensified, and to those among his companions who responded to him, and they inflicted upon him and them various kinds of harm. This is the way of God, Mighty and Majestic, with His creation, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾ [Fussilat: 43]. And He said: ﴿Thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 112]. And He said: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman." Did they bequeath this to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 52-53].

So He, glorified is He, consoled His Prophet with this, and informed him that he has an example in those messengers who preceded him. And He consoled his followers by His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the example of those who passed away before you? They were touched by misfortune and adversity and were shaken until the messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the victory of God?" Unquestionably, the victory of God is near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214].

The seeker has no end to his seeking and no slackening in his aim. Rather, his aim is more complete, his seeking more perfect, and his intention more sincere. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And worship your Lord until certainty ("al-yaqin") comes to you﴾.

Here "certainty" means death, by the consensus of the people of Islam. So when death came to him (ﷺ), his will, aim, and intention were at their highest peak and in their full perfection and completeness. Where, then, is the defect in this will?

The defect and deficiency lie in a will whose source is the self (nafs) and desire (hawa), and whose goal is to attain the seeker's own share (hazz) from the Beloved. Even if the Beloved wills that too, the seeker loves something else more than it: that his aim be purely the right of his Beloved and the attainment of His good pleasure, annihilated (fani) from his own share of his Beloved. Indeed, his share from his Beloved becomes the very right of his Beloved and His aim. This is the will and love that has no defect and no deficiency.

We ask Allah the Exalted to bestow His grace upon us and to give us life, even if only with a soul (nafs) of this kind, just as He bestowed the teaching and knowledge of it. Indeed, He is Generous and Bountiful.

Ibn al-Qayyim, after a lengthy discussion on the station of annihilation (fana'), said:

One of them says: "Whoever witnesses the Reality (haqiqa), the command (amr) falls from him." They argue with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you﴾ [Al-Hijr: 99], and they interpret "certainty" as witnessing the cosmic decree (al-hukm al-kawni), which for them is the Reality.

There is no doubt that the common believers are better than these people and sounder in faith, for this is zandaqa (heresy) and hypocrisy (nifaq), and a lie on their part against themselves, their Prophet, and their God.

As for their lie against themselves: they must inevitably make a distinction, so they turned away from the prophetic and Qur'anic distinction and fell into a natural, instinctive distinction (al-farq al-nafsi al-tab'i). They are like Iblis, who was arrogant about prostrating to Adam and was content for himself to lead the sinners of his offspring. They are like the polytheists, who were arrogant about worshipping Allah, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and were content for themselves to worship stones, trees, the dead, and idols. They are like the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'a), who were arrogant about following the texts (nusus) and receiving guidance from their niche of light, and were content for themselves to follow opinions that oppose the innate nature (fitra), reason ('aql), and the Law (shar'), considering them rational certainties and preferring them over the texts of the Prophets. In reality they are doubts that contradict both revelation (sam') and reason.

They are like the Jahmiyya, who declared the Lord transcendent above His Throne and placed Him in the innards of houses, shops, and bathhouses, saying: "He is in every place in His essence." They declared Him transcendent above the attributes of His perfection and the qualities of His majesty, out of fear, in their claim, of anthropomorphism (tashbih), and so they likened Him to inanimate, deficient, base things that do not speak, have no hearing or sight, no knowledge or life. Rather, they likened Him to non-existent things whose existence is impossible.

They are like the Mu'attila, who said: "Above the Throne there is nothing but non-existence. Above the Throne there is no Lord to be worshipped, no God to whom one prays and prostrates, no hands are raised to Him, Jesus was not raised to Him, the angels and the Spirit do not ascend to Him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not taken up to Him, he did not draw near to Him until he was two bow-lengths away or nearer, nothing descends from Him, nothing ascends to Him, and the people of Paradise will not see Him above them on the Day of Resurrection. His istiwa' (settling) upon His Throne has no reality, but is only a metaphor (majaz) that may be negated. His highness above His creation is by rank and honor, not by essence. Likewise His being above is a being above by dominance (qahr), not a being above in essence." They declared Him transcendent of the perfection of His highness and His being above, and described Him with what makes Him equal to non-existence and the impossible. They said: "He is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither joined to it nor separated from it, neither in contact with it nor distant from it, neither within us nor outside us."

It is well known that if one of them were asked, "Describe non-existence for us," he would describe it with exactly this.

The application of this negation to pure non-existence is closer to intellects and natures than its application to the Lord of the Worlds, in whose creation there is nothing of His essence, and in whose essence there is nothing of His creation. Rather, He is separate from His creation, settled upon His Throne, high above all things, and above everything.

The point is that whoever turns away from some part of the truth and denies it inevitably falls into a falsehood corresponding to what he turned away from and denied. Even in deeds: whoever turns away from acting for the sake of Allah alone, Allah tests him with acting for the sake of creatures. He turns away from acting for One whose harm, benefit, death, life, and happiness are in His hand, and is tested with acting for one who does not possess any of that for him.

Likewise, whoever turns away from spending his wealth in obedience to Allah is tested with spending it for other than Allah, and he does so unwillingly.

Likewise, whoever turns away from toiling for Allah is tested with toiling in the service of creatures, inevitably.

Likewise, whoever turns away from guidance by revelation is tested with the refuse of opinions, the rubbish of minds, and the filth of thoughts.

Let whoever wants to advise his own soul, its happiness, and its success reflect on this point, in himself and in others.

There is no doubt that the common believers, despite their heedlessness and their desires, are sounder in faith than these people, provided they do not nullify the command and the prohibition. For faith together with distinction and heedlessness is better than witnessing and collectivity (jam'iyya) accompanied by the corruption of faith and its stripping away.

As for their lie against their Prophet: their belief is that his standing in prayer and his litanies and acts of worship were only for the sake of legislating, not because they were obligatory for him, since that obligation had fallen from him by witnessing the Reality and the perfection of certainty. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him and all His messengers to worship Him until the end of their lifetimes. He said: ﴿And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you﴾ [Al-Hijr: 99], and it is death by consensus, as He said in the other verse about the disbelievers: ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment until certainty came to us﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 46]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Uthman ibn Maz'un, certainty has come to him from his Lord," and he said this when Uthman died. And the Messiah said: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet, and He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾ [Maryam: 30–31].

This is Allah's charge to the Messiah, and likewise to all His prophets and messengers and their followers. Al-Hasan said: "Allah has not made for His believing servant any term (ajal) other than death."

When these people combine the denial of Allah's names and attributes (tajahhum) with the witnessing of the Reality and standing at it, may Allah protect you from the complete nullification of the Lord and His Law, so that no Lord is worshipped and no Law is followed at all.

Whoever wants to stand on the reality of what we have mentioned, let him let his gaze roam among those landmarks, stand at those sites, and ask the conditions, the traces, and the signs. If they do not answer him with speech, they will answer him with their state and lesson.

Only one who keeps company with the travelers, separates from those who sit idle, takes up faith, and parts from the habits of the people of his time will believe this, and will not be content with the saying of the one who said:

Leave lofty aims, do not rise to pursue them;
sit down, for you are the one who eats and clothes himself.
